entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Roger of Cannae was an Italian bishop born in unknown year and died on December 30, 1129. He played a crucial role as the Bishop of Bari from 1108 to 1111. The Catholic Church honours him as a saint.

Roger's influence can be seen in the establishment of the Order of Preachers (Mendicants), founded by his contemporary, St. Francis of Assisi, with whom he shared spiritual ideas and practices. Roger also contributed to the development of the Benedictine Rule, which became a cornerstone of monastic life.

His legacy extends through the preservation of several medieval manuscripts, including those containing works by Dante Alighieri, Petrarch, and other notable writers of the time. These texts provide valuable insights into the intellectual and cultural landscape of 12th-century Italy.

The ruins of the Church of San Nicola, where Roger is buried, serve as a testament to his lasting impact on the spiritual heritage of the region.

"The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want." - St. Augustine (attributed)

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Roger of Cannae played a crucial role in shaping the spiritual landscape of medieval Italy, influencing the development of the Benedictine Rule and contributing to the establishment of the Order of Preachers (Mendicants). His legacy extends through his veneration by pilgrims and locals alike, as well as the preservation of medieval manuscripts containing works by notable writers.
